elements.id-string-7: Even though trained mainly on images, we discover that pretrained diffusion models show impressive power in guiding sketch synthesis.In this paper, we present DiffSketcher, an innovative algorithm that creates \textit{vectorized} free-hand sketches using natural language input.DiffSketcher is developed based on a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model.It performs the task by directly optimizing a set of Bézier curves with an extended version of the score distillation sampling (SDS) loss, which allows us to use a raster-level diffusion model as a prior for optimizing a parametric vectorized sketch generator.

elements.id-string-28: In this work, we present DiffSketcher, an algorithm that can synthesize novel and high-quality free-hand vector sketches based on natural language text input.
elements.id-string-29: DiffSketcher does not require any text-to-sketch training pairs or large datasets of sketches.
elements.id-string-30: Instead, with the guidance of a pretrained diffusion model~\cite{ldm_2022_Rombach}, we define a sketch as a set of Bézier curves and optimize the curves' parameters through a differentiable rasterizer~\cite{Li_2020_diffvg}.
elements.id-string-31: The key idea behind DiffSketcher is to transfer the prior knowledge from text-to-image generation model into the differentiable rasterizer.
elements.id-string-32: This allows the optimization of text-guided sketches with semantic consistency, ensuring that the final output sketches are coherent and aligned with their corresponding text inputs.
elements.id-string-33: However, it is a non-trivial task to fully leverage the pre-trained diffusion model to efficiently generate high-quality free-hand sketches for both simple objects and complex scenes.
elements.id-string-34: To this end, we propose three strategies to improve the generation quality and efficiency:

elements.id-string-70: In this section, we provide a concise overview of diffusion models, which are a class of generative models that utilize latent variables to gradually transform a sample from a noise distribution to a target data distribution~\cite{diffusion_models_dickstein_2015,ddpm_ho_2020}.
elements.id-string-71: Diffusion models consist of two components: a forward process $q$ and a reverse process or generative model $p$.
elements.id-string-72: The forward process, which is typically modeled as a Gaussian distribution, gradually removes structure from the input data $x$ by adding noise over time.
elements.id-string-73: The reverse process, on the other hand, adds structure to the noise starting from a latent variable $\mathbf{z}_t$.
elements.id-string-74: Specifically, the generative model is trained to slowly add structure starting from random noise $p(\mathbf{z}_T) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$ with transitions $p_{\phi}(\mathbf{z}_{t-1}|\mathbf{z}_{t})$.
